title: Direct Observation of Electron Tunneling from Plasmonic Nanostructures under Electron Beam Irradiation
content: Electron emission from plasmonic nanostructures has emerged as a promising avenue for diverse applications, ranging from advanced electron microscopy to novel plasmon-driven electron sources [1-4]. The advent of ultrafast laser technology has facilitated the generation of intense electric fields capable of directly inducing field emission [3]. This process, governed by Fowler-Nordheim (FN) theory, predicts an exponential increase in field-emitted conduction electrons with increasing field strength [5]. Plasmonic systems further amplify this emission due to the strong localization of evanescent fields at nanoscale hotspots [6, 7]. Particularly in coupled plasmonic nanostructures with sub-nanometer gaps, extreme field enhancement at these hotspots reduces the requirement for high-intensity driving fields [5, 8]. While FN tunneling is indirectly estimated from gap volumes in coupled metal nanoparticles [9], the direct observation of tunneling field emission under electron beam irradiation has remained elusive. Despite extensive research in high-voltage and laser-driven systems, realizing field electron emission from electron-beam-irradiated plasmonic nanostructures has been hampered by experimental limitations and the lack of appropriately designed emitter structures.
